summary.intent: Add a printed message to the memory-loop refresh command showing which branch/scope it is operating on.
summary.outcome: Added a scope print statement to `runMemoryLoopRefresh` in `memory_loop_cmd.go` that displays e.g. `Scope: repo (branch: main)` or `Scope: me (alishakawaguchi)` before loading sessions. Change was committed.

repo: The memory-loop refresh command uses a `resolveMemoryLoopScope` helper that returns a `memoryLoopScope` struct containing either a `Branch` or `OwnerID` field.
The `refresh` subcommand lives under `memory-loop`, not under `insights` — there is no top-level `refresh` command.

code.finding: resolveMemoryLoopScope returns a memoryLoopScope with Branch or OwnerID; scope print was added after this call in runMemoryLoopRefresh.

workflow: User interrupted an initial broad search and clarified the target command, avoiding wasted exploration of insights_cmd.go.

friction: Initial ambiguity about which command 'refresh' referred to caused exploration of insights_cmd.go before the user clarified it was the memory-loop refresh command.
implementation_rationale: Print the resolved scope immediately after `resolveMemoryLoopScope` so the user always sees which branch/owner the refresh is targeting, aiding debugging and transparency.
codebase_patterns: Scope resolution is centralized in `resolveMemoryLoopScope`; consumers read `.Branch` or `.OwnerID` from the returned struct to determine context.
